text: Write a method that returns a function, capturing a value in the process. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: static ___ { return ___; }              // returns a function that adds n
explanation: Verified: 6 then 101. `n` lived in `adder`'s stack frame, which was destroyed when `adder` returned, and the lambda still has it because the value was copied in. That is a closure — and it is also, exactly, an object with one field and one method. Chapter 25 said our interpreted language lacked this; here is Java doing it, and the two are the same mechanism.
